# Seeing when nvsnap fails

Status: proposed. §1 is built (the agents' ServiceMonitor renders by
default, and every agent exports `nvsnap_build_info`); §2 to §6 are not.

## Problem

When nvsnap fails a capture or a restore, the function usually still
comes up: admission starts the next pod cold. Nobody sees that it
happened, and when a failure does reach the user, nothing points at
nvsnap.

nvsnap does record each failure, in four places, and each loses it:

| Where | What it holds | Why nobody sees it |
|---|---|---|
| The agents' `/metrics` (`internal/metrics/lifecycle.go`) | Every capture, restore and admission outcome, with a failure reason | Scraped only where an operator turned the ServiceMonitor on by hand. An agent's counters reset when its pod restarts |
| Pod events (`NvsnapCaptureFailed`, `NvsnapRestoreFailed`, `NvsnapCaptureRefused`) | One per failure, on the pod | The platform replaces the pod within minutes, and the event store keeps events for an hour |
| `NvsnapFunction` (`internal/fnstatus`) | Per configuration: state, restore failures, GPU faults, stalls, a reason | The counts, with no time and no failed pod; nothing alerts on it |
| The agents' summary log lines | One line per capture, restore and pod start | Only someone who already suspects nvsnap reads them |

Some cold starts nvsnap chooses are counted nowhere. When the webhook
declines to restore a single pod's CRIU capture, it logs and starts the pod
cold (`internal/webhook/criu_restore.go` `criuRestoreFor`). It does this in
three cases:

- the pod names its own instance;
- the capture belongs to another tenant scope;
- the checkpoint failed to restore before.

The instance path counts the same decisions as `admissions_total{decision="cold"}`
with a reason (`internal/webhook/criu_group.go`).

On a regression run against a test cluster, the suite reported failures
that do not occur with nvsnap off. For two of them, the user saw only:

| Test failure | What nvsnap had done |
|---|---|
| A 504 | Captured the function's only pod while it served |
| An instance terminated for "no capacity" | Pinned a cold start to a node with no free GPU |

Attributing them meant reading agent logs by hand, and the one record
that named the cause had already expired.

## What a failure is

Metric names below are the exported ones (`nvsnap_` prefix).

| Kind | Source today | Counted as |
|---|---|---|
| A capture failed | `nvsnap_capture_outcomes_total{outcome="failed"}`, event | failed |
| A capture never served after restore | `{outcome="unverified"}`, no event | failed |
| A configuration cannot be captured | `{outcome="refused"}`, event | refused, not failed: a known limit with a reason |
| A pod never started under gpushare | `{outcome="gpushare-failed"}`, no event (`observeGPUShareFailed`) | failed |
| A cachedir capture failed, as a CRIU fallback | `{method="cachedir",outcome="failed"}`, no event (`observeCachedirCapture`) | failed |
| A cachedir capture failed, in cachedir mode (the chart's default) | logged by `runCapture` (`internal/rootfsonly/watcher.go`), not counted | failed |
| A restore ran and failed | `nvsnap_restore_outcomes_total{outcome="failed"}`, event | failed |
| A restored pod failed after its restore | logged by `failRestored` (`internal/agent/restored_watch.go`), not counted | failed |
| A restore could not run (fetch, placeholders) | `{outcome="not-run"}`, event | failed after its retries |
| A restore failed on a faulty GPU | `{outcome="gpu-fault"}` | not nvsnap's, counted apart (`docs/design/GPU-FAULT-PROBE.md`) |
| A pod that could restore started cold | `nvsnap_admissions_total{decision="cold"}` on the instance path; not counted on the single-pod path | failed when the reason is nvsnap's (§2) |
| A capture whose restores stalled `criuGroupMaxStalls` times | not counted: `parseCRIUGroup` reports no capture, and its pods start cold uncounted | failed (§2) |
| An admission error the webhook turned into "admit unchanged" | logged by `Handler.Decide` (`internal/webhook/admission.go`, "fail-open"), not counted; the API server sees a success | failed |
| A lookup error `Mutate` logged and continued past (model volume, election) | logged, not counted | failed |
| A cachedir restore whose cache seeding failed | not observed: the seed step runs in the pod, and in cachedir mode the agent's restore observer (`startCRIUAutoRestore`) does not run. Unverified: whether the seed step still exits 0 after a failed copy | failed |
| A pod admitted with the gpushare fallback | `nvsnap_admissions_total{decision="fallback",reason="gpushare-failed"}` | failed: follows a gpushare failure |
| A rank of a captured instance admitted without nvsnap | `nvsnap_admissions_total{decision="missed"}`, with reason `opted-out` or not | failed unless opted out |
| The webhook unreachable | nothing nvsnap counts; the API server's webhook metrics | failed (§4) |

## Design

### 1. The history is scraped

Built. `agent.metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled` defaults to `auto`: the chart
installs the agents' ServiceMonitor wherever the cluster serves the
ServiceMonitor API. It carries the namespace and labels this repository's
collectors select by (`docs/operate/METRICS.md`).

The agents' counters now outlive the agents. With the cluster's
Prometheus forwarding them, they also outlive the cluster.

### 2. Every cold start nvsnap chose is counted

The single-pod CRIU path counts each cold start it chooses as
`nvsnap_admissions_total{decision="cold"}`, with the reasons the instance
path uses:

| Where | Decline | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `criuRestoreFor` | The pod names its own instance | `own-instance` |
| `criuRestoreFor` | The capture belongs to another tenant scope | `scope-mismatch` |
| `criuRestoreFor` | The checkpoint failed to restore before | `checkpoint-blocked` |
| `Mutate`, after `criuRestorePatches` fails | The pod cannot be prepared as the placeholder | `prepare-failed` |

Every error that leaves a pod admitted without what nvsnap meant to give
it counts as `decision="error"` with the error's class. That covers:

- errors `Handler.Decide` turns into an unchanged admission;
- errors `Mutate` logs and continues past (`internal/webhook/mutate.go`:
  the model-volume and election lookups), counted where they are caught.

- errors the CRIU lookups turn into "no capture": `lookupCRIUGroupFor`
  (a namespace read) and `lookupCRIUGroup` (a record read) return false on
  any error today. The lookup result tells an error from an absent capture
  and from an exhausted one (below), and the error is counted.

A cache miss (the backend answers "not found") is not an error and is not
counted.

The instance path gains one: a complete capture whose restores stalled
`criuGroupMaxStalls` times. `parseCRIUGroup` reports it as no capture at
all today, so `criuGroupRestorePatches` returns before it counts. The
lookup tells a stalled capture from an absent one and counts the cold
start with reason `stalls-exhausted`.

The reasons split two ways:

- **Ones the pod's author chose** (`own-instance`) are expected.
- **Ones that mean an earlier failure** (`checkpoint-blocked`, `prepare-failed`, `model-unavailable`) count against nvsnap.

`docs/operate/METRICS.md` lists which is which. The alerts in §4 use that list.

### 3. The function keeps its failures

Each function version gets one failure record, whatever its capture
method and whether it ever captured: the ConfigMap
`nvsnap-failures-<name>` in nvsnap's namespace, where `<name>` is the
version's `NvsnapFunction` name (`fnstatus.ObjectName`: the version id, or
`ns-<namespace>` outside NVCF). It is labelled with the function's
identity, as `record_identity.go` labels group records.

The history does not live on the capture records:

- **Not every function version has one.** A standalone CRIU capture has
  only a manifest. A cachedir capture has only its manifest
  (`nvsnap-capture-<hash>`), written on success, with no function
  identity. A function version can restore a capture it never made.
- **Capture records are rewritten.** A capture's takeover
  (`claimGroupRecord`) and its completion (`captureGroup`) replace a group
  record's data.
- **Capture records are deleted with their capture**
  (`retirableCachedirCaptures`).

A record of its own avoids all three.

The record holds the last 10 failures, newest first. Each entry holds:

- the time;
- the kind (from the table above);
- the reason class (the metric's `reason` label);
- the configuration (the capture key), when there is one;
- the pod (namespace/name and UID) and node;
- the first 256 bytes of the message. The full message stays in the event
  and the agent's log, which can hold up to 16 KiB (`groupReasonMax`).

An entry is appended by whoever observes the failure:

| Kind | Written by |
|---|---|
| Capture failed, unverified, gpushare-failed; cachedir capture failed, in either mode | the agent that ran the capture (`captureGroup`, `observeGPUShareFailed`, `captureFallbackRank`, `runCapture`) |
| Standalone CRIU capture failed | the agent, at the outermost caller of `Agent.Checkpoint` (the server's `runCheckpoint` through `checkpointHandler`); a checkpoint that `captureGroup` invoked is recorded once, by `captureGroup` |
| Shared cache set not collected or not refreshed | the agent's model volume controller (`tryCollect`, `tryRefresh`), where it calls `Cache.RecordFailure` after its last attempt; admissions then compile locally |
| Restore failed, not run, failed after restore (`failRestored`) | the agent that ran it |
| Cachedir restore whose seeding failed | the agent on the pod's node, from a result file the seed step writes, through an observer that runs in cachedir mode too |
| Cold start nvsnap chose, admission error (§2) | the agent on the pod's node, from the pod's `nvsnap.io/admission` annotation |
| The same, for a pod no node has taken | nvsnap-server, from the same annotation, once the pod has been unschedulable for 60 seconds or is deleted without a node |

**Admission decisions are written onto the pod.** The webhook does not
write the record from admission:

- A background write would be lost if the agent stopped before it
  committed.
- A synchronous write would make admission wait on the API server.

Instead, the webhook's own patch annotates the pod with its decision:
`nvsnap.io/admission: cold/checkpoint-blocked`, or `error/<class>`.
Where it would otherwise admit the pod unchanged after an error, it
returns a patch carrying only that annotation. The pod carries the
decision for as long as it exists. The agent on its node appends it once
per pod UID, so a restarted agent replays what it had not written.

**Pods no node takes.** Admission comes before scheduling, so a pod that
stays pending (no node has a free GPU, say) has no agent to record its
decision, and that is one of the failures the record is for. nvsnap-server
runs once per cluster and already watches pods. It appends the decision of
an annotated pod with no `spec.nodeName` once the pod's `PodScheduled`
condition has been `False` for 60 seconds, or when the pod is deleted
before any node took it. The entry names the pod UID and the scheduler's
reason (`Unschedulable` and its message). Entries are keyed by pod UID: a
pod scheduled after the server wrote its entry is not appended again by
its node's agent, and the server skips a UID already on the record. The
server's ClusterRole reads ConfigMaps today; it gets `create` and `update`
on them, in nvsnap's namespace only (a Role).

**Writers race.** Several agents can append to one record at once, so each
append is a read, then an update conditioned on the record's
`resourceVersion`, retried on conflict (`retry.RetryOnConflict`). An append
that fails for any other reason is retried with backoff (1 s to 30 s, for up
to 5 minutes), then logged. The failure is still counted (§4).

**Projection.** `internal/fnstatus` projects the record onto the version's
`NvsnapFunction`:

- as `failures`, each entry under its configuration when it names one;
- as `lastFailure` at the top.

`kubectl get nvsnapfunctions` shows a `LAST-FAILURE` column, the age of
`lastFailure`. A version with failures and no capture gets an
`NvsnapFunction` too, with no configuration.

**Retention.** The reaper deletes a failure record once its newest entry is
older than the retention period and no capture record of the version
remains. Ten entries of at most about 400 bytes each keep the record under
4 KiB.

### 4. Alerts ship with the chart

A `PrometheusRule`, under its own `agent.metrics.rules.enabled` (`auto`,
`true`, `false`). `auto` renders it when the cluster serves
`monitoring.coreos.com/v1/PrometheusRule`, independently of the
ServiceMonitor: a cluster can discover monitors without evaluating rules.
The `deploy/stacks/observability` stack, for one, turns PrometheusRule off
and stores metrics outside Prometheus. Where the rules are evaluated, and
by what, is an open question.

The alerts rely on two changes in the agent:

- **A failure counter with fixed labels.** `nvsnap_failures_total{kind}`
  counts every failure in the table above by kind. The agent creates each
  kind's series at 0 when it starts, and the outcome counters keep their
  open `reason` label for diagnosis.

  `increase()` alone misses the first failure when Prometheus first sees
  a series already at 1, as it does when the failure comes before an
  agent's first scrape. A series merely missing from an earlier sample
  does not prove it is new; a scrape gap looks the same. And an agent's
  restart must not discard what its previous process had counted.

  So the counter carries a `boot` label, the process's start time, and the
  agent exports `nvsnap_agent_start_time_seconds{boot}`. A rate needs the
  same accounting for its denominator: `nvsnap_restores_total{boot,result}`
  counts every restore that ran or could not run (`result` is `ok` or
  `failed`), created at 0 at start like the failure counter. Each process is
  then its own series, and each series is judged by its own age:

  ```promql
    (increase(nvsnap_failures_total[w])
       and on (instance, boot)
       (time() - last_over_time(nvsnap_agent_start_time_seconds[w]) >= w))
  or
    (max_over_time(nvsnap_failures_total[w])
       and on (instance, boot)
       (time() - last_over_time(nvsnap_agent_start_time_seconds[w]) < w))
  ```

  A process older than the window is counted by `increase()`; one that
  started within it, by its highest count. A restarted agent's previous
  process keeps its own series, still counted. The two halves never match
  the same series, so `or` cannot keep one side's zero over the other's
  count. The label adds one series per kind per agent restart; they go
  stale with their process.
- **`nvsnap_build_info` from every agent.** Built: it used to be set only
  under the CRIU capture method.

| Alert | Fires when |
|---|---|
| `NvsnapRestoreFailing` | Over 30 minutes, more than 20% of `nvsnap_restores_total` is `result="failed"`, and at least 3 failed; both counted with the expression below |
| `NvsnapCaptureFailing` | 3 or more failed, unverified or gpushare-failed captures in an hour |
| `NvsnapUnexpectedCold` | Any cold or fallback admission with a reason that counts against nvsnap, in 30 minutes |
| `NvsnapAdmissionErrors` | Any `decision="error"` admission in 15 minutes. These reach the API server as successes, so no webhook metric sees them |
| `NvsnapRankAdmittedWithout` | Any `missed` admission whose reason is not `opted-out`, in 15 minutes |
| `NvsnapWebhookUnreachable` | The API server's calls to the nvsnap webhook fail (`apiserver_admission_webhook_request_total` with an error code, or its rejection count), in 15 minutes. `missed` cannot detect an outage: it is counted only for ranks of an instance whose leader the webhook did admit |
| `NvsnapGPUFault` | Any faulty GPU probe result |
| `NvsnapAgentsUnscraped` | For 15 minutes, any of: the agents' targets report `up == 0`; fewer agents export `nvsnap_build_info` than the agent DaemonSet has ready pods (`kube_daemonset_status_number_ready`, where kube-state-metrics is scraped); no agent exports it at all. One silent node fires it, not only all of them |

The thresholds are a starting point, to be checked against at least a week
of scraped history before any alert pages. Severity and routing labels are
NVCF SRE's to set; the rule ships them as values with no default (open
questions). Each alert links its section of a troubleshooting page
this work adds under `docs/operate/`.

### 5. A test run says what nvsnap did

A regression suite run answers "did nvsnap fail anything, and in which
test" without anyone reading logs:

- **Per test, at the end of the run.** Each test records its function
  version ids and its start and end times. Once every test is done, the
  suite reads each version's `NvsnapFunction` (named by the version id,
  `fnstatus.ObjectName`) and attaches to each test the `failures` entries
  timed within its run and naming a pod in its namespace. A failed test
  whose function has such an entry says so in its report.

  Reading at the end, not at each test's teardown, leaves time for the
  record's writes (retried for up to 5 minutes) and nvsnap-server's
  projection (every 30 seconds by default). Failure records outlive the
  test's function, so nothing is lost by waiting. A version whose record
  is still being written when the suite reads is reported as
  "attribution incomplete" when the per-run count below exceeds the
  entries found.
- **Per run.** At the end, the suite queries the cluster's metrics over the
  run's window and prints, next to the pass/fail summary:
  - nvsnap failures by kind, with §4's expression, so an agent that started
    during the run and failed before its first scrape is counted;
  - the API server's failed calls to the nvsnap webhook. An unreachable
    webhook counts nothing in nvsnap, and an instance none of whose pods
    reached it counts no `missed` admission either.

This needs no new nvsnap endpoint. The change is in the suite: a teardown
hook and a final step.

### 6. The platform shows it

NVCA reads `NvsnapFunction` and reports nvsnap's last failure in the
function's deployment details, as it reports a pod's last error today.
That puts it in front of the function's owner, so it ships:

- behind an NVCA flag that defaults off;
- with NVCF SRE's go-ahead;
- with the customer notice the release process needs.

It comes after §1 to §5 have run on test clusters long enough to show the
reasons are right.

## Why not

- **A new nvsnap API for failures** (on nvsnap-server or the agents). The
  record and the metrics already hold the facts; a third store would
  disagree with them.
- **Longer event retention.** A cluster-wide setting nvsnap does not own,
  and events still go with their namespace.
- **Per-function labels on the metrics.** One series per function version
  grows without bound; the record holds the per-function view instead.
- **Failing the pod when nvsnap fails.** Starting cold is right for the
  user; the failure has to be visible, not fatal.

## Limits

- **A pod with no function identity** (outside NVCF, in a namespace the
  agent cannot name) has no failure record; its failures reach the metrics
  and events only.
- **History ends with retention.** A failure record is deleted once its
  newest entry is older than the retention period and the version has no
  capture left. The metrics keep the counts.
- **A pod deleted before its node's agent sees it** takes its admission
  annotation with it. Its admission is still counted (§4).
- **The alerts need scraped metrics and a rule evaluator.** On a cluster
  without the ServiceMonitor API, only §3 and the per-test half of §5 work.
- **An agent restart loses the counts since its last scrape.** At a
  30-second scrape interval, a failure in the last 30 seconds before a
  restart can go uncounted. The failure record keeps it.

## Tests

| Section | Test |
|---|---|
| §2 | An error `Handler.Decide` admits unchanged, and a model-volume or election lookup error `Mutate` continues past, count `decision="error"`; a cache miss does not; each of the four single-pod declines, and the instance path's `stalls-exhausted`, increments `nvsnap_admissions_total` with its reason; a stalled capture is told from an absent one |
| §3 | Each kind in the table appends one entry through its writer, including `failRestored`, the cachedir watcher and the seed result; two concurrent appends both land; a non-conflict API error is retried; the list keeps the newest 10; the projection keeps the order and `lastFailure`; a version with failures and no capture is projected |
| §4 | `nvsnap_failures_total` has every kind at 0 after start; repeated fail-open admissions answered with HTTP 200, with no instance leader admitted, fire `NvsnapAdmissionErrors`; `promtool test rules` for every alert, firing and not firing, three failures before the agent's first scrape followed by several unchanged scrapes (counts 3), 20 successful and 3 failed restores before the first scrape (13%: `NvsnapRestoreFailing` does not fire), old failures followed by a long scrape gap and no new failure (must not fire), failures scraped before an agent restart and none after (still counted), one of two agents going silent, and missing data; the chart renders the rule only where the cluster serves the API |
| §3, every capture kind | A failure is on the version's failure record and projects onto `NvsnapFunction`, for: a CRIU group capture, a standalone CRIU capture (once, also when a group capture invoked it), a shared cache set that was not collected or refreshed, a cachedir-mode capture, a failed seed whose workload still starts, and a version that restores a shared capture it never made. The record survives a recapture and a reaper pass |
| §3, admission | A cold start's `nvsnap.io/admission` annotation is appended once per pod UID; an agent restarted between the admission and the append replays it; a fail-open error admits the pod with only the annotation; a pod unschedulable for 60 seconds, and one deleted with no node, is appended by nvsnap-server with the scheduler's reason; a pod scheduled after the server's append is not appended again by its agent |
| §5 | Against a test cluster: a run with a deliberately blocked checkpoint reports the `checkpoint-blocked` cold start under its test, and not under a later test of the same function; a failure-record write delayed past 60 seconds is still attributed; a run with the webhook made unreachable reports the API server's failed calls |

## Open questions

- Severity, routing and whether any alert pages: NVCF SRE.
- Which rule evaluator runs the alerts on clusters whose collector does not
  evaluate PrometheusRules: NVCF SRE.
- Where the cluster's metrics are forwarded, and whether nvsnap's are on
  by default everywhere: NVCF SRE.
- Whether §6 reports to the function's owner or only to operators.
